timeplay.title: Games for cinema audiences
intro: Timeplay ran a platform in Cineplex theatres where the audience plays on their phones, in sync with the big screen, before the movie starts. Led a small team building the games, both branded titles for advertisers on fixed campaign deadlines and the platform's own trivia and party formats.
Each entry is a short capture of the game running on the theatre screen. "Big screen and controller" means the audience's phones drove the game; "big screen" titles played out on the screen alone.

blackcherry.title: Four educational titles
intro: BlackCherry was an Ottawa studio building commissioned educational games in Unity. Joined straight out of school and shipped four titles there across web, tablet, and mobile, from prototyping through launch support.

studio.title: Installations and experiments
studio.employer: Carleton University, Algonquin College, and personal work
studio.cover_alt: A hand playing a Novation Launchpad, pads lit red, yellow, and green in a dark room
intro: Student and personal projects from the Interactive Multimedia and Design program and the years just after: a five-screen projection arena, a touch table for sound synthesis, 3D modelling and rigging, an animated short, and the music setup that still runs in the background.

powerplay.title: PowerPlay
text: PowerPlay was Timeplay's themed trivia format for the pre-show: the audience answers on their phones, the big screen keeps score, and the theme changes per campaign, from sci-fi movie rounds to a sponsor's brand.
The stills are themed rounds and screens from the leaderboard, buzz-in, order-up, pick-three, reveal-it, and head-to-head modes.

first-encounters.title: First Encounters

videos.caption: Extensive gameplay video showing the majority of the learning modules and other core mechanics.

text: First Encounters is a media learning experience consisting of a rich online game, an extensive video and music gallery, and detailed teacher's guides. The game and website are the culmination of over a year's worth of research and development, providing an in-depth look at life in North America when Europeans began arriving from across the Atlantic.

Carleton University's Centre for Indigenous Research, Culture, Language and Education (CIRCLE), in partnership with Heritage Canada's Canadian Content Online Program, commissioned the project to retell the story of first contact between the Norse and the Thule circa 1000 CE, and the French and the Mi'kmaq in the 1500s.

Started on prototyping and code development, then moved to the learning modules for each culture and how they shaped the overall gameplay. Also helped develop the bilingual features and integrated a large portion of the interface and 3D assets.

virtual-safety-village.title: Virtual Safety Village

videos.caption: The essential gameplay throughout the town.

text: Virtual Safety Village was commissioned by the Sault Ste. Marie Safe Communities Partnership. It is a 3D interactive game that lets kids learn the proper way to navigate everyday hazards in the home and on the street, in a secure online environment.

The objective is to catch a malfunctioning safety robot that is wreaking havoc in the player's home and neighbourhood by making everything it touches unsafe. With the help of safety goggles, the player assesses the hazards the robot has created, like a hairdryer placed too close to water, and chooses the right course of action. The learning outcomes centre on electrical, bicycle, railroad, and fire safety.

Integrated all interface and 3D assets and programmed the gameplay for each learning area, including character and camera controllers, path systems for the bike and cars, character and item customization, menu interfaces, and audio-visual cues throughout. Also optimized the game for iOS and Android, although it shipped as a web game.

sid-the-science-kid.title: Sid the Science Kid

videos.caption: The essential gameplay from the Lever and Measurement mini-games.

text: Two games developed by BlackCherry for The Jim Henson Company, deployed on the Vinci Tab, a custom Android tablet for young children. As lead programmer, integrated the interface audio, 3D assets, and gameplay mechanics. The Sid the Science Kid characters were animated with 2D sprite sheets; the Vinci characters were 3D.

In the lever game, players help Gerald build a lever to get his toys into the sandbox, and come away with a basic understanding of how a lever works. In the measurement game, players help Gabriella find and measure everyday objects using non-standard units, and learn relative length by measuring things themselves.

one-million-monkeys.title: One Million Monkeys
text: Million Monkeys is about building silly stories with friends: collaborate a few words at a time, overcome tricky rules, and earn bananas for satisfying a set of brain-bending criteria. Bananas raise your rank, add stickers to your stories, and lift limitations.

BlackCherry built the game with Beeline Interactive through a four-month service contract in 2012, responsible for all of production from art direction through programming, on Beeline's concept. It shipped free-to-play on iOS and Android.

Worked mainly on the social layer, letting players invite friends and share stories through Facebook, Game Center, Twitter, email, or the device's contacts. Built several custom menu tools on NGUI in Unity, and spent a large share of the schedule debugging before and after launch and implementing feature requests.

hexrayvision.title: Sanctuary
hexrayvision.client: Carleton University senior project, team Hexrayvision
text: Sanctuary was a team senior project at Carleton University, an interactive installation built over two terms. The team constructed an arena with five rear-projection screens for a 300-degree high-definition field of view, 720 by 10,000 pixels.

For interaction, the team built a laser tracking system using infrared cameras to manipulate 3D objects projected on the screens, sent controller signals as OSC messages over the network to track multiple screens, and built a motion recognition system as a second control mechanism.
The gameplay itself was built in Unity, with particle systems, physics, deferred lighting, and a custom five-camera rig to handle the resolution.

wicka-wicka.title: Wicka Wicka
text: A group project from a design studio at Algonquin College: a collapsible multimedia touch table built around sound synthesis. Tracking software reads symbols on the underside of physical markers and displays musical instruments on the table surface.

Multiple fingers can play pianos, scratch records, and adjust modulators. MIDI is sent on to studio production software and visualizers. Built with Processing and OpenGL, with FL Studio 8 on the sound side.

robot-battle.title: Robot Battle

videos.caption: Animation playblast with the rigs still in progress, showing the IK setup in grey, rig handles in blue, and spline handles in red.

text: A character-driven animated short made for a 3D modelling course, inspired by early mecha series like Gundam Wing and Neon Genesis Evangelion. Since the project ran over one semester, robotic characters were a deliberate choice: easier to animate than anything organic. Once animation started, simplified the camera angles and environment to keep the focus on movement.

The rigs were the interesting part: simple but mechanically accurate. The arms and legs use inverse kinematics with extra handles for parts like the shoulder plates; the monster's tail is a spline with several handles for full control over curve and twist.

trojan-warfare-ii.title: Trojan Warfare II
text: Trojan Warfare started in Design Studio IV with no prior Unity experience on the team. As gameplay programmer, built the asset import, physics, player controls, and enemy AI. Ben King and Dane Clarke made the character and environment assets, and Mark Pintar handled the menu system, website, and marketing.

dhalsim.title: Dhalsim
text: A character model for a 3D modelling course. The brief was to model a character of choice with specific parts of the body in detail, then texture and rig it for animation.
Picked Street Fighter's Dhalsim for his expressive face and a muscular build that made the body straightforward. The focus was the face, ears, and hands.

star-castle.title: Star Castle
text: A castle model for a 3D modelling course. The brief was to design and model a castle in a chosen style; this one went futuristic, inspired by the band Starcastle and the artwork of their 1976 self-titled album.

sound-table.title: Sound Table
text: Music has been a constant alongside games. Sound Table was the first finished track from a setup built around Ableton Live 9 with Operator, a Novation Launchpad, and a rack of Korg pads (the nanoSeries 2, KaossPad 3, KaossPad Quad, Kaossilator Pro, and the minis).
The chain runs the Korg pads through a TC Electronic Impact Twin into Ableton and onto the Launchpad, which controls how each looped clip launches, with per-track volume and pan on the nanoKontrol.

voxie-tactics.title: Voxie Tactics
voxie-tactics.type: Free-to-play turn-based tactics · Windows, iOS, Android
text: A free-to-play turn-based tactics game shipped to three platforms as a live service. Senior developer from the first commit of the Unity version, working with the lead developer on technical direction.

Set up the Unity project, ported the legacy C++ codebase to C# and Unity, and built the modular voxel avatar system, with characters assembled from parts and a bulk conversion tool that brought the art library across.

Brought battles onto Netcode for GameObjects with server-authoritative actions, then built the dedicated game servers on Unity Multiplay and the matchmaking behind them. Later moved server hosting to Rocket Science with a custom allocator in Cloud Code.

Took the PC launcher and patcher from proof of concept to production, with S3 distribution, per-environment builds, and a Windows installer. Built the in-game store with in-app purchases on mobile and PC, and wired up analytics, remote config, Datadog logging, and crash reporting.

Designed the studio's git flow and the GitHub Actions pipelines behind every client and server build, which carried straight over to Hyperflora. Over three years the studio shipped seasonal content and new game modes, including Titan Arena, on top of it.

creatubbles.title: Super Code Strike
creatubbles.type: Creative platform for kids · voxel tools
text: Creatubbles is a creative platform for kids. Built and maintained the voxel art pipeline from authoring tool to runtime, a character customization system with a large outfit and accessory library, a user-facing level editor, and procedurally generated voxel terrain.
Also prototyped new mechanics with design on a regular cadence.

invent-dev.title: VR architectural configurator
invent-dev.type: VR application · HTC Vive and Oculus
text: A VR application for customizing architectural designs: change home layouts, place furniture from a tagged library with filters, and see it rendered at high fidelity. Architected the application, designed and implemented the UI and UX for layout changes and furniture placement, built the furniture library and its filtering, implemented the high-definition rendering paths, and designed the system for backend integration.

casino.title: Casino platforms
casino.type: Multiplayer poker console · mobile slot platform
text: Two contracts in the same year. At Cloud Street Gaming, owned the art pipeline and asset integration for a multiplayer poker console deployed in live casinos, built the post-processing systems, designed game flow and animations, and overhauled the UI and UX while keeping the game logic running.
At WGames, maintained a mobile slot-game platform, integrated art into the game templates, and rebuilt the system that loads games.
